run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T00:51:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Frontend's RequestErrorRate alert is corroborated by its own error spans: the frontend ERROR-status span rate was 0 through 00:43:49, first became nonzero at 00:45:49 (0.0140/s), and rose to a peak of 1.3615/s at 00:55:49, spanning gRPC client calls to CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder plus the /api/cart and /api/checkout routes. The deepest observed fault is a Chaos Mesh stress experiment on the cart datastore: a Chaos Mesh Schedule named otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh spawned StressChaos experiments every minute from 00:50:43 to 00:58:28, and those experiments record 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft/valkey-cart'. The valkey-cart container was OOMKilled (exit code 137, finished 00:54:48), has restartCount 4 and is now in CrashLoopBackOff with BackOff events from 00:51:47, its pod is not Ready, and the valkey-cart Deployment reports no available/ready replicas. The cart service itself logs 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' and error status lines, and its error spans are its own server spans POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, GetCart and EmptyCart. Frontend, cart and the valkey-cart pod are the entities with their own failure evidence; other otel-demo deployments are ready 1/1 and the nodes report no memory or disk pressure. Because the Schedule object's spec cannot be read with the available Kubernetes kinds (its Spawned/Forbid events are the only evidence tying it to the injected stress), and the exact stress parameters and creation time are not visible, the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: Frontend's own ERROR-status span rate was 0 from 00:27:49 to 00:43:49, first nonzero at 0.0140/s at 00:45:49, then 0.0842 at 00:47:49, 0.6526 at 00:49:49, 0.8246 at 00:51:49 (the minute the alert fired), and peaked at 1.3615/s at 00:55:49 before declining to 0.5125 at 01:01:49.

The frontend's error spans are concentrated on cart and checkout paths: at 5-minute resolution (reporting from 00:51:36) the largest error-span rates were 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' (0.363/s at 00:55:36), POST /api/cart (0.296), grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (0.193), grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (0.170), and smaller rates on POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder.

The cart service has its own ERROR-status spans on its server operations POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (0.0932/s at 00:55:36, 0.2085 at 01:00:36, 0.1281 at 01:05:36), POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (0.0914, 0.1740, 0.0921) and POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart (0.0019 at 01:00:36).
Cart's error-span rate (5-minute rate) first became nonzero at 00:52:36 (0.0208/s), rose to 0.3693/s at 00:55:36 and peaked at 0.5671/s at 00:59:36.

The cart service container logs record connection failures to its datastore during the window: 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' first appears in the retrieved cart log window at 00:54:47.634 and repeats, interleaved with lines 'Error status code {StatusCode} with detail {Detail} raised.' from 00:54:05 through 00:55:55.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft (owned by ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c) is Running but not Ready: container valkey-cart shows lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at 00:54:48 (started 00:54:37), restartCount 4, and state.waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff; its memory limit is 10Mi (request 4Mi).

Kubernetes events for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft show Warning BackOff 'Back-off restarting failed container valkey-cart' 22 times from 00:51:47 to 00:59:05, and 6 'Created container: valkey-cart' / 'Started container valkey-cart' events from 00:14:17 to 00:56:23, i.e. repeated container starts during the incident.

A Chaos Mesh Schedule named otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh spawned StressChaos objects named otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress-<suffix> at 00:50:43, 00:51:43, 00:52:43, 00:53:43, 00:54:43, 00:55:43, 00:57:33 and 00:58:28, with Normal 'Spawned' events reading 'Create new object: otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress-...' and Warning 'Forbid' events when a previous experiment was still running.

Those StressChaos experiments name the target explicitly: events on otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress-flgz4/ckxt6/w8p5x/nt6th/95xf6 read 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft/valkey-cart' (Started at 00:50:43, 00:51:43, 00:52:43, 00:53:43, 00:54:43 and TimeUp/Recovered about 55s later), and later experiments (ltcpd, psc57) log Warning 'Failed to apply chaos: ... no running task found' because the container was restarting.

Kubernetes state at query time: Deployment valkey-cart has 1 desired replica but no available and no ready replicas, while the cart Deployment is 1/1 available and ready and all other otel-demo Deployments are 1/1; of the 21 pods in otel-demo, only valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is not Ready (4 restarts), all others are Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

Frontend-proxy has its own ERROR-status spans during the same interval: the 'ingress' error-span rate rose from background levels (0.0088/s at 00:40:36) to 0.3333/s at 00:55:36, 0.9877/s at 01:00:36 and 0.6906/s at 01:05:36, with a smaller rise on 'router frontend egress' (0.0772, 0.1018, 0.0258).

Cart traffic degraded beyond the general load decline: cart's total span rate fell from 18.82/s (00:45:36) to 12.61/s (00:55:36) and 1.71/s (01:05:36), while the frontend's unset-status span rate over the same period fell only from 47.72/s to 41.18/s to 14.20/s.

A healthy trace captured at 00:29:59 (before the errors) shows the call structure frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' (client, grpc status 0) -> cart 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' -> cart 'HGET', i.e. cart's server span calls into a datastore via HGET.

Node-level resource exhaustion is not supported: all five nodes report MemoryPressure=False and DiskPressure=False, so the valkey-cart OOMKill is container-level (10Mi limit) rather than a node condition.

Rejected as the trigger: a load/traffic ramp on the frontend. The frontend's unset-status span rate had already plateaued near 47-50/s from 00:37:49 and was declining (41.18/s by 00:55:49) while the frontend error rate rose from 0.0140/s at 00:45:49 to 1.3615/s at 00:55:49, so error onset does not track the load ramp.

Rejected as the cause: the cart Deployment being down or misconfigured at the deployment level. The cart Deployment is 1/1 available and ready and its pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 is Running/Ready with 0 restarts; the failures originate below it in its valkey-cart datastore.

The frontend alert is a downstream consequence of cart failures caused by the valkey-cart OOMKill/CrashLoopBackOff: frontend error spans are on CartService/AddItem, GetCart and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client spans and /api/cart routes, and cart's own error rate and connection-failure logs rise in the same 00:50-01:00 interval. Trace-level proof for the incident window is missing (Jaeger holds no spans after 00:29:59).

The valkey-cart OOMKills are produced by the Chaos Mesh stress experiments, not by steady-state valkey memory usage: each Schedule spawn names the valkey-cart container as the target, the campaign runs 00:50:43-00:58:28, and the container's last termination is OOMKilled with exit 137 while its limit is only 10Mi.

Advisory: the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh should be reviewed/paused if this fault injection is not intended, and valkey-cart's 10Mi memory limit (requests 4Mi) should be raised to a realistic value, after which the valkey-cart pod's readiness and cart's error logs should be re-checked.

gaps: The Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress and its StressChaos objects are not readable with the authorized Kubernetes kinds, so the injected stress parameters (memory size, duration, mode), the Schedule's creation/modification time and whether it is still active are unknown; only its events were evidence.

The alerting rule behind RequestErrorRate is not visible: list_prometheus_rules returned no data for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the exact expression and the reported value 3.0222 could not be reproduced.

Jaeger returned no traces for the incident window (its newest returned spans are at 00:29:59, data_as_of 2026-11-18T00:29:59.763663), so the frontend-to-cart error traces and span error details for 00:50-01:10 are unknown; only Prometheus span metrics cover that interval.

Frontend errors first became nonzero at 00:45:49, several minutes before the first recorded Schedule spawn at 00:50:43; that early low-rate portion (0.0140-0.0842/s) has no identified cause in the evidence.
The cart container log query kept only the newest 100 of 137 matching lines (00:45:00-00:56:00), so earlier connection-failure lines before 00:54:05 in that interval were not read.

Old pod cart-9fd895bb7-m7zfz (previous cart ReplicaSet) shows Warning FailedKillPod and 75 Killing events ending 00:49:38, i.e. it changed during the window, but it is not in the current pod list and its relation to this incident is unresolved.

No metric for kube_pod_container_* or rpc_* was returned by the metric discovery queries, so per-container restart counters, memory usage and RPC client/server error metrics could not be used (unknown, not zero).
next_steps: Review the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-valkey-memory-stress in namespace chaos-mesh (spec, duration, target selector) and decide whether the valkey memory stress should continue.
Raise the valkey-cart container memory limit above 10Mi and verify the pod reaches Ready with a stable restartCount.
Re-check the RequestErrorRate rule definition in the alerting stack to confirm which metric produced the 3.0222 value.
After the datastore recovers, confirm cart and frontend error-span rates return to 0 and reset the frontend alert.
Follow up separately on the stuck terminating pod cart-9fd895bb7-m7zfz and its FailedKillPod events.
